- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (≤ 0.2), model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak to avoid overcorrection.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of downward bias correction in forecast.
- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.8) and model is flat or rising slowly, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day moving average of history, adjust forecast to align with recent trend, not just historical mean.
